title: Promotion first, features late: Apple settles Siri lawsuit for $250 million
excerpt: The flashy demo at the launch event never became a real feature, and Apple is ultimately settling the score with money. According to MacRumors on Nov. 21 local
content_html:
The flashy demo at the launch event never became a real feature, and Apple is ultimately settling the score with money. According to MacRumors on Nov. 21 local time, lawyers representing consumers filed court documents on Nov. 16: in a $250 million (about 1.673 billion yuan) settlement pool, eligible users are expected to receive at least $61 (about 408 yuan) per iPhone, with a maximum of $95.

A flashy demo promised big; the delay made Apple a defendant

The dispute dates back to June 2024. Apple painted a new picture of Siri in its demos: understanding personal context, being aware of on-screen content, and deeply controlling apps. It also promoted these features through launch events, its website, and TV ads. But in March 2025, the personalized Siri was announced to be delayed, and consumers quickly filed a class-action lawsuit accusing Apple of false advertising. Apple denies all allegations and says the settlement is only meant to avoid the costs and risks of prolonged litigation.

Base payout of $25; the more claims, the less each gets

Under the payout rules, each eligible device has a base payout of $25. The final amount will fluctuate based on the total number of valid claims, capped at no more than $95; if too many people file claims, it could even fall below $25. The legal team currently estimates it will be at least $61, but if claim volume rises sharply, the actual payout will shrink further. Eligibility is also strict: you must be a U.S. resident, have bought the phone in the U.S. between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, and not for resale; only seven models qualify: iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, and the iPhone 16 series. Claims must be filed by Dec. 21, 2026; the settlement approval hearing is scheduled for Feb. 24, 2027; and payments are expected to begin in 2027.
